answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy should require a slashable bond and a multi-epoch voyage of independently attested answers and grades before an identity can harbor spendable rewards. Empty clones are cheap to register but sit like unused sable ink: dark on the page, worthless until peers countersign uncorrelated work. When voting patterns match across aliases, the shared bond is slashed as one body, so headcount farming loses more than it can earn.
